COFINFAD: Colombian Fintech Financial Analysis

Author

Ng Meng Ye

Project Overview & Background

The Objective

The objective of this project is to understand the behaviors behind customer transactions and how socio-demographic factors—such as age, income, and occupation—affect customer transactions. By applying statistical correlation techniques, we aim to identify which personal attributes are the true drivers of financial activity within the Colombian fintech ecosystem.

Analytical Framework: Socio-Demographic Correlation

To isolate the influence of these factors, we utilize a Correlation-First approach:

  1. Metric Derivation: We normalize the data by calculating the Average Transaction Value (Total Volume / Count) to move beyond surface-level totals and understand the “per-action” behavior of different groups.

  2. Non-Parametric Testing: Recognizing that income and transaction data are often heavily skewed, we employ Spearman’s Rank Correlation (via ggstatsplot) to assess the strength of relationships between demographic variables and transaction intensity.

  3. Faceted Comparison: We utilize faceting to determine if socio-demographic correlations remain consistent across different segments, or if certain groups (e.g., specific age brackets or genders) exhibit unique behavioral outliers.

Our Data

The dataset captures this transition from traditional cash-based behavior to a digital-first economy.

  • Customer Profiles: Includes 54 variables that allow us to see how demographics (like the income_bracket or location) correlate with tx_count and avg_tx_value.

Data Preparation

Raw .csv files are converted to .rds format to fit within GitHub’s 100MB limit while maintaining high-speed loading in R.

library(tidyverse)

customer_raw <- read_csv("data/customer_data.csv")

saveRDS(customer_raw, "data/customer_data.rds")

customers <- readRDS("data/customer_data.rds")

The code chunk below will be used to install and load these packages in RStudio.

pacman::p_load(ggstatsplot, plotly, DT, scales,tidyverse,gtsummary,ggdist, ggridges, ggthemes,colorspace)

Data Cleaning

We only keep those columns that are required for our analysis

  1. customer_id
  2. age
  3. gender
  4. location
  5. income_bracket
  6. education_level
  7. household_size
  8. marital_status
  9. tx_count
  10. avg_tx_volume
  11. total_tx_volume
library(tidyverse)

# Retaining only the specified columns
customers_cleaned <- customers %>%
  select(
    customer_id,
    age,
    gender,
    location,
    income_bracket,
    education_level,
    household_size,
    marital_status,
    tx_count,
    avg_tx_value,
    total_tx_volume
  )

Create age group

customers_cleaned <- customers_cleaned %>%
  mutate(age_group = case_when(
    age <= 35 ~ "20-35", # Assuming the youngest users start around 20
    age >= 36 & age <= 50 ~ "36-50",
    age >= 51 & age <= 65 ~ "51-65"
  )) %>%
  # Re-ordering the factors for the plot
  mutate(age_group = factor(age_group, 
                            levels = c("20-35", "36-50", "51-65")))

Create household_size group

customers_cleaned <- customers_cleaned %>%
  mutate(hh_group = case_when(
    household_size == 1 ~ "1",
    household_size >= 2 & household_size <= 3 ~ "2-3",
    household_size >= 4 & household_size <= 5 ~ "4-5",
    household_size >= 6 ~ "6+",
    TRUE ~ "Unknown"
  )) %>%
  # Set levels to ensure the plot follows the correct order
  mutate(hh_group = factor(hh_group, 
                           levels = c("1", "2-3", "4-5", "6+")))

Review the statistical summary of the spending behaviours

library(gtsummary)
library(gt)

continuous_summary_table <- customers_cleaned %>%
  select(tx_count, avg_tx_value, total_tx_volume) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd}) | {median} ({p25}, {p75}) | [{min}, {max}]"
    ),
    digits = all_continuous() ~ 0, # Financial volumes don't need decimals
    label = list(
      tx_count ~ "Transaction Count (Frequency)",
      avg_tx_value ~ "Average Transaction Value (COP)",
      total_tx_volume ~ "Total Transaction Volume (COP)"
    )
  ) %>%
  modify_header(label = "**Financial Metric**") %>%
  as_gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Financial Performance Descriptive Statistics",
    subtitle = "Summary of User Transaction Behavior (2023)"
  ) %>%
  opt_stylize(color = "blue", style = 1)

Analyzing how different categories affects the Transaction Amount vs. Frequency behavior

  1. Education Level
  2. Marital Status
  3. Gender
  4. Age

1. Education Level

Visualizing distribution using half eye graph and boxplot

plot_distribution <- function(cat_var) {
  
  ggplot(customers_cleaned,
         aes(x = {{cat_var}}, 
             y = avg_tx_value)) +
    
    stat_halfeye(
      adjust = 0.5,
      justification = -0.2,
      .width = 0,
      point_colour = NA
    ) +
    
    geom_boxplot(
      width = 0.20,
      outlier.shape = NA
    ) +
    
    stat_dots(
      side = "left",
      justification = 1.2,
      binwidth = 0.5,
      dotsize = 2
    ) +
    
    labs(
      x = deparse(substitute(cat_var)),
      y = "Average Transaction Value",
      title = paste("Distribution of Average Transaction Value by", 
                    deparse(substitute(cat_var)))
    ) +
    
    theme_minimal()
}
plot_distribution(education_level)

Visualizing distribution using half eye graph and boxplot on a Log Scale (Base 10)

plot_demo_log <- function(cat_var) {
  
  ggplot(customers_cleaned, 
         aes(x = {{cat_var}}, 
             y = avg_tx_value, 
             fill = {{cat_var}})) +
    
    stat_halfeye(
      adjust = 0.5,
      justification = -0.2,
      .width = 0,
      point_colour = NA
    ) +
    
    geom_boxplot(
      width = 0.20,
      outlier.shape = NA
    ) +
    
    scale_y_log10(
      labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M"),
      name = "Avg Transaction Value (COP) - Log Scale"
    ) +
    
    labs(
      title = paste("Socio-Demographic Analysis (Log-Transformed):",
                    deparse(substitute(cat_var))),
      x = deparse(substitute(cat_var))
    ) +
    
    theme_minimal()
}
plot_demo_log(education_level)

Correlation Analysis (relationship between average transaction value vs transaction count (frequency)

options(scipen = 999)

plot_behavior_correlation <- function(a) {
  ggscatterstats(
    data = customers_cleaned, 
    x = avg_tx_value,  
    y = tx_count,
    type = "nonparametric", 
    title = paste("Socio-Demographic Factor Analysis:", a),
    xlab = "Average Transaction Value",
    ylab = "Transaction Frequency"
  ) + 
    facet_wrap(vars(!!sym(a))) +
    # This part cleans the x-axis
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M"),
      breaks = seq(0, 50000000, by = 10000000) # Optional: set breaks every 10M
    )
}
plot_behavior_correlation("education_level")

Confirmatory Data Analysis

Oneway ANOVA Test: ggbetweenstats() method

In the code chunk below, ggbetweenstats() is used to build a visual for One-way ANOVA test on Average Transaction Amount by different variables.

1. Education Level

ggbetweenstats(
  data = customers_cleaned,
  x = education_level,
  y = avg_tx_value,
  type = "nonparametric",
  ylab = "Average Transaction Value",
  xlab = "Education Level",
  title = "Average Transaction Value by Education Level",
  mean.ci = TRUE, 
  pairwise.comparisons = TRUE, 
  pairwise.display = "s",
  p.adjust.method = "fdr",
  messages = FALSE
)

Significant Test of Association (Depedence) : ggbarstats() methods

1. Education Level

In the code chunk below, the Maths scores is binned into a 4-class variable by using cut().

customers_cleaned <- customers_cleaned %>% 
  mutate(Average_Transaction_bins = 
           cut(avg_tx_value, 
               breaks = c(0, 1339108, 4658605, Inf),
               labels = c("Low Spend", "Medium Spend", "High Spend"))
)

In this code chunk below ggbarstats() is used to build a visual for Significant Test of Association

ggbarstats(customers_cleaned, 
           x = Average_Transaction_bins, 
           y = education_level)

2. Marital Status

           x = Average_Transaction_bins, 
           y = marital_status)
